column2: Paste before every Portrait Art Direction: "Stylized fantasy character portrait for a visual-novel style dialogue screen, painterly digital art with clean bold shapes and soft cel-shaded lighting, matching a whimsical, expressive young-adult indie RPG card game. A single character shown from the waist up, centered, turned three-quarters toward the viewer, expressive face and clear readable silhouette, soft key light from the upper left. Same framing and scale for every character: top of the head about 8% from the top edge. Fully transparent background (PNG); if transparency isn't possible, use a plain flat light-gray background with nothing else. No text, no dialogue box, no frame, no border. 2:3 portrait, 1024x1536."

When the player talks to an NPC, their portrait pops up beside the dialogue box (like the reference images). Save each portrait as its Portrait Image ID (e.g. NPC-ELDER.png). Optional expressions use a suffix: NPC-ELDER_HAPPY.png, NPC-ELDER_ANGRY.png, etc.; the game falls back to the base portrait if an expression is missing. Vendor screens use a separate shop background (Vendor Screens section below) with the vendor's portrait composited on top.
